cities.base: South Congress area, walkable for the one night on each end and close to the airport
cities.name: Austin

cities.base: Main Street guesthouse or B&B, the center of gravity for the wine road and Enchanted Rock
cities.name: Fredericksburg

cities.base: day trip / evening stop from Fredericksburg
cities.name: Luckenbach, TX
LBJ National Historical Park / LBJ Ranch

places.name: Wimberley Square
places.note: Small central square with shops and galleries around a gazebo. Pleasant for twenty minutes after Blue Hole, not a place to build hours around.

places.name: Crystal River Winery
places.note: Smaller and less crowded than Becker or William Chris, good if you want a quieter third stop instead of a big name.

places.name: Auslander Biergarten
places.note: German and Texan menu, good beer list, patio seating. Loud and touristy but the schnitzel is solid; closed Wednesdays.

places.name: Hill Country Herb Garden
places.note: The old Fredericksburg Herb Farm, now Hill Country Herb Garden: small gardens, a spa, a restaurant and the Marigold gift shop for soaps and dried herbs. Closed Monday, later hours Wednesday to Saturday; skip it if you are not into it, it is not a real garden visit.

places.name: William Chris Vineyards
places.note: Reservation-only on weekends, walk-ins turned away. Solid Texas-grown fruit, better than most on this stretch.

places.name: Becker Vineyards
places.note: Lavender fields out front in season, one of the older and bigger producers on 290. Gets full on weekends, arrive right at opening.

places.name: National Museum of the Pacific War
places.note: Large and well done, built around Nimitz's boyhood connection to Fredericksburg; the $26 ticket covers the Nimitz and George H.W. Bush galleries, and the Pacific Combat Zone closes at 15:00. Closed Tuesday, and it eats a half day if you actually read the exhibits.

places.name: Vereins Kirche Museum
places.note: Small octagonal building in the town square, a 1934 replica of the 1847 original torn down in 1897; quick stop rather than a destination. Open Monday to Saturday 10:00 to 17:00, and the same $12 day pass covers the Pioneer Museum.

places.name: Fredericksburg Main Street
places.note: Nutt Street to Adams Street stretch, shops in restored limestone buildings. Real cost is bakeries and beer gardens, not the walk itself.

places.name: Rainey Street Historic District
places.note: Bungalow houses converted to bars, more relaxed and less frat-heavy than Sixth Street proper. Good for a low-key first or last night drink, skip Sixth Street itself, it's stag-party loud and not distinct to Austin.

places.name: Texas State Capitol
places.note: Free self-guided or guided tours, pink granite building bigger than the US Capitol dome. Fine as a quick stop, not worth rearranging a day around; open 07:00 weekdays and 09:00 weekends, to 20:00.

places.name: Blanton Museum of Art
places.note: Solid rainy-day option, university art museum with a good rotating collection, rarely crowded compared to the outdoor sights. Closed Monday, open to 20:00 on Saturday; check the price, the ticket was not confirmed in dollars.

places.name: Congress Avenue Bridge Bats
places.note: Largest urban bat colony in North America, they emerge at dusk roughly March through October. Free to watch from the bridge or the bank below, weather and season dependent, check a bat forecast before counting on it.

places.name: Lady Bird Lake Hike and Bike Trail
places.note: Paved loop along the lake, good early walk or run before it gets hot, decent skyline views from the pedestrian bridges.

places.name: Zilker Metropolitan Park
places.note: Big green space around Barton Springs, good for a walk or to let kids run before or after the pool. Nothing you'd drive across town for on its own.

places.name: Barton Springs Pool
places.note: Spring-fed pool, 68F year round, genuinely cold even in August heat; $9 for a non-resident adult. Thursdays it shuts for cleaning from 09:00 to 19:00, and 05:00 to 08:00 is unguarded swim at your own risk.

places.name: Suerte
places.note: Modern Mexican, handmade masa, good first-night or last-night dinner without needing a car. Reserve ahead, it's small and popular; dinner from 17:00 (to 23:00 Friday and Saturday), and weekend service starts at 11:00.

places.name: la Barbecue
places.note: Shorter line than Franklin, same quality brisket and sausage, trailer with picnic tables. Better choice if you don't want to sacrifice a whole morning; closed Monday and Tuesday, open 11:00 to 18:00 the rest of the week.

places.name: Franklin Barbecue
places.note: Line forms before dawn and they sell out most days by early afternoon. Worth it once if you're willing to queue, otherwise skip and eat elsewhere, this isn't a relaxed dinner option. Closed Mondays; open Tuesday to Sunday 11:00 to 15:00 or sellout, and the $30 a head is a guess to check.

places.name: South Congress Avenue
places.note: Strip of shops, boutiques and food trailers running north from Elizabeth St to the river. Good for an arrival evening when you're jetlagged and just want to walk and eat, don't try to do the whole street.

places.name: LBJ National Historical Park / LBJ Ranch
places.note: Free self-guided driving tour with a free permit from the LBJ State Park visitor center in Stonewall (08:30 to 16:00); the Texas White House has been closed for repairs since 2018, so there is no house tour. Skip it if presidential history doesn't interest you.

places.name: Luckenbach, TX
places.note: Dance hall, general store, and a porch with pickers most evenings. Free to enter, cover charges for bigger shows. Not a full night out, a couple of beers and live music.

places.name: Enchanted Rock State Natural Area
places.note: Day passes are $8 for 13 and up and can be booked up to 30 days ahead; on weekends and holidays the gate closes to walk-ins once the park is full, so reserve rather than turn up with cash.

places.name: Blue Hole Regional Park
places.note: Cypress-lined swimming hole on Cypress Creek, rope swings and cold spring-fed water. Swimming runs from May 1 (closed now, back 1 May 2027), by reservation only, with half-day passes from $15; arrive at the start of your slot for parking and a quiet stretch of bank.

places.name: Cypress Creek Nature Trail
places.note: Short flat loop connected to Blue Hole park, shaded by cypress. Good for stretching legs before or after swimming, not a destination on its own.

places.name: Wimberley Market Days
places.note: Runs the first Saturday of the month, March through December, at Lions Field. Craft vendors and food stalls. Only worth routing for if your trip lines up with the actual Saturday.

places.name: Jacob's Well Natural Area
places.note: Artesian spring famous for its deep blue-green pool over a submerged cave system; free to visit and park, open daily 08:00 to 18:00 with no entry after 17:30. Swimming is seasonal and by reservation and often shut when flow is low, so check before driving out.

places.name: Mill Creek BBQ
places.note: Straightforward Central Texas barbecue, brisket and sausage by the pound. Good lunch stop before or after Blue Hole, not fancy and doesn't try to be.

places.name: The Leaning Pear
places.note: Farm-to-table lunch spot by the square with a shaded patio. Salads, sandwiches and wood-fired pizza, a decent sit-down break in the heat; closed Monday and Tuesday, busy on weekends.

places.name: Blanco River at Scudder's Falls
places.note: Small limestone ledges and pools on the Blanco River with camping rentals nearby. Quieter alternative to Blue Hole when it is booked out, though access can depend on river level and whether you are a paying guest of the camp.

places.name: EmilyAnn Theatre and Gardens
places.note: Small outdoor amphitheater and garden with a peacock enclosure. A quiet, low-key stop if you have extra time, not worth a special trip on its own.

places.name: Wimberley Glassworks
places.note: Working glassblowing studio and gallery, you can watch pieces being made through large windows. Free to visit, good rainy-afternoon filler that isn't just another shop.

places.name: Toonie's Warehouse Studio
places.note: Local bar and event space with occasional live music, a genuine small-town hangout rather than a tourist bar. Only worth it if you are staying in Wimberley itself rather than day-tripping, which for this trip you are not, so treat as optional.

places.name: Wimberley Zipline Adventures
places.note: Skip. It eats half a day and is generic zipline-park fun you could do in a dozen US towns, not specific to the Hill Country and it competes directly with your Blue Hole time on an already long day-trip day.

places.name: Front Side crevice and cave area
places.note: Small crevice climb near the base, easy detour on the way up, skip if you're pressed for time since the summit itself is the real destination.

places.name: Stargazing on the dome
places.note: Designated Dark Sky site, genuinely dark skies with little light pollution. Only realistic if you're staying late or camping, not compatible with the half-day plan from Fredericksburg unless you go back out for it.

places.name: Summit at sunset
places.note: Same trail as the morning summit hike but timed for sunset, genuinely good light over the Hill Country. Means hiking down in the dark, bring a headlamp, and the park has a hard closing time so check it.

places.name: Bouldering on the main dome
places.note: Informal bouldering is popular on the lower faces, no permits needed, bring your own gear. Not a maintained climbing area, ask rangers about closures for raptor nesting in spring.

places.name: Cave Formations near Echo Canyon
places.note: Small boulder caves and crevices along the trail, kids like scrambling through them, nothing dramatic, don't go out of your way for it alone.

places.name: Enchanted Rock Visitor Center
places.note: Small exhibit on the geology and Tonkawa history of the rock, worth five minutes if you're waiting for the gate or need water and a bathroom. No separate ticket, it is included in the $8 park entry, but check the price.

places.name: Turkey Pass / Vista Loop
places.note: Short connector with views back toward the main dome, good add-on if you have extra time after the summit and don't want a full second trail.

places.name: Moss Lake
places.note: Small pond along Echo Canyon Trail, mostly dry in drought years. Not a swimming spot, just a rest point and photo stop, don't plan around water being there.
places.neighborhood: East side near Echo Canyon junction

places.name: Loop Trail
places.note: 4.25 miles, mostly flat, circles the whole park through woodland and creek crossings. This is the one to do when wind or heat closes off climbing the dome, minimal elevation gain.

places.name: Echo Canyon Trail
places.note: About 2.4 miles round trip connecting to Loop Trail, rockier and less crowded than the Summit Trail, some scrambling through boulders. Good option if you already did the summit and want more.

places.name: Summit Trail
places.note: 0.6 miles one way but steep granite dome, about 425 ft gain, 1.5-2 hrs round trip with photo stops. No shade at all, do it before 10am. Rock gets too hot to touch by midday in summer.

places.name: Nixta Taqueria
places.note: Michelin Bib Gourmand taqueria with pink-corn tortillas nixtamalized in house; order the duck carnitas taco, the tuna tostada and the duck-fat refried beans. Dinner Tuesday to Sunday, lunch only Friday to Sunday, closed Monday, and early arrival beats the walk-up wait.

places.name: Bullock Texas State History Museum
places.note: Opened in 2001, it tells Texas from the Spanish era to oil across three floors; $17 for adults, and the IMAX and special exhibits cost extra. A short walk up Congress from the Capitol, so do them the same morning.

places.name: LBJ Presidential Library
places.note: Gordon Bunshaft's ten-storey travertine block on a 30-acre site, full of the papers, photos and phone recordings of Johnson's career; give it two hours. Open daily, and check the price, the ticket was not confirmed in dollars.

places.name: Harry Ransom Center
places.note: Free, and it holds a Gutenberg Bible and the first photograph ever made, Niepce's view from a window, on permanent display. Closed Monday; weekends it opens at noon.

places.name: Umlauf Sculpture Garden and Museum
places.note: Charles Umlauf's bronzes and stone pieces across 4 acres of garden and ponds, some you are allowed to touch; pair it with Barton Springs next door. Closed Monday, weekends from 11:00, and check the price, the ticket was not confirmed in dollars.

places.name: French Legation State Historic Site
places.note: The 1841 house of France's envoy to the Republic of Texas, one of the oldest buildings in Austin, on 2.5 acres. Hours vary, check, and check the price before you go.

places.name: O. Henry Museum
places.note: Free, the 1886 cottage where William Sydney Porter lived, furnished to the period with his piano and his hand-drawn maps. Open Wednesday to Sunday from noon only.

places.name: Texas State Cemetery
places.note: Set up in 1851, with Stephen F. Austin and Albert Sidney Johnston among the graves; walk it early before the heat. No admission is listed, so check the price, open daily 08:00 to 17:00.

places.name: The Driskill Hotel
places.note: Cattle baron Jesse Driskill's hotel, opened Christmas 1886 behind the largest arched doorway in Texas; walk the lobby and have a drink at the bar. No ticket, but nothing says free, so check.

places.name: Mount Bonnell
places.note: A 750 ft summit with Lake Austin and the skyline below; reviewers report free parking and entry, but check. Parking fills on busy days, so go on a weekday or early.

places.name: Eaker Barbecue
places.note: Texas barbecue with Korean touches: order the gochujang pork ribs, the bulgogi sausage and the kimchi fried rice, then the bourbon banana pudding. Wednesday to Sunday from 11:00 until it sells out, so get there before 13:00.

places.name: Cabernet Grill
places.note: The one nice dinner: a Texas-only wine list, Angus steaks from $37 for the strip to $62 for the filet, Gulf seafood and crab-shrimp cakes. Book weekends ahead; closed Sunday and Monday, and some weeknights it closes at 20:30.

places.name: Pioneer Museum
places.note: A 3.5-acre yard of 19th-century German settler buildings, starting with the 1849 Kammlah house; the $12 day pass also covers the Vereins Kirche. Closed Sunday.

places.name: Fort Martin Scott State Historic Site
places.note: The first US Army post on the Texas frontier, with the restored commander's quarters, barracks and blacksmith shop; $10 since September 2025. Closed Sunday and Monday.

places.name: St. Mary's Catholic Church
places.note: Leo Dielmann's limestone Gothic Revival church of 1908, on the site of the 1848 wooden one. Tours run on Sunday after the 9:00 and 11:15 Masses and otherwise by appointment; hours vary, check, and check the price.
places.neighborhood: Historic district (304 W San Antonio St)

places.name: Marktplatz
places.note: The town square around the octagonal Vereins Kirche, free to wander; start here and walk out along Main Street.

places.name: Pioneer Memorial Library (old courthouse)
places.note: Alfred Giles built it in 1881-82 as the second Gillespie County courthouse from stone quarried outside town; a court until 1939, a free public library since 1967. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Cross Mountain Park
places.note: The settlers found a timber cross on this 1,951 ft hill in 1847 and called it Kreuzberg; the lit cross is from 1946, replaced in 2024. Free, dawn to dusk, and the climb to the top is 10 to 15 minutes.
places.neighborhood: N Milam St, north edge of town

places.name: Zion Lutheran Church
places.note: Six families built this limestone church from 1854 with their own hands and stone; the bell tower and cruciform plan came in 1908. No visiting hours or price published, so hours vary, check, and look from Main Street if it is shut.

outings.why: The granite summit loop is only 1.5-2 hours round trip but the drive, entrance line, and heat push it to a half day; book the $8 day pass ahead, since the gate closes to walk-ins when the park is full.
outings.name: Enchanted Rock summit loop
outings.season: year-round, go at opening in summer to beat the heat
outings.fallback: Walk the lower loop trail and skip the summit scramble if it's too hot or crowded.

outings.why: The Stonewall to Fredericksburg stretch has tasting fees of $15-25 per stop; two or three wineries is the right pace, not five, and the well-known ones require weekend reservations.
outings.name: US-290 wine road tasting
outings.season: year-round, fall wine season in October is the busiest

outings.why: A dance hall, a general store, and a porch with live music; free to enter but it is a couple of beers and songs, not a full night out.
outings.name: Luckenbach evening

outings.why: A free self-guided driving tour of the LBJ ranch near Stonewall, permit from the state park visitor center; the Texas White House is closed, so skip it if presidential history doesn't interest you.
outings.name: LBJ Ranch driving tour

outings.why: 1.5 hours each way from Fredericksburg makes this a long day; cold, clear water worth the drive once, but swimming is by reservation only from May 1, with half-day passes from $15.
outings.name: Blue Hole swim, Wimberley
outings.season: swim season from May 1, reservations required
outings.fallback: Skip if the drive feels too long that day; there is no closer substitute.

outings.why: Spring-fed and cold even in August, a good last activity before an early flight.
outings.name: Barton Springs Pool swim

destination.name: Texas Hill Country
destination.pitch: A driving trip through German-town food and wine along 290, granite hiking and swimming holes, bookended by Austin's springs.
destination.caveat: This is a car trip with no walkable center, so distances between wineries, swimming holes, and towns eat real chunks of every day. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Austin bookends the trip with South Congress for one night on each end.
because.food: German-town bakeries, beer gardens, and the 290 wine road give this a food identity distinct from the rest of Texas.
because.nature: Enchanted Rock's granite dome and the cold spring-fed swimming holes are the physical heart of the trip.
because.relaxation: Barton Springs and Blue Hole are unhurried cold-water afternoons, not activities to rush.
